 Celebrity Health Nicole Taylor, One of the Identical Triplets Behind Country Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35
 The singer was diagnosed with aggressive breast cancer in 2022 after finding a lump she said felt like “a little AAA battery.” Nov. 3, 2026, 9:35 AM EST / Source : TODAY Rachel Paula Abrahamson 
 Why Survivor-to-Survivor Breast Cancer Support Matters 08:20 Share Add TODAY to Google Nicole Taylor, a member of the country music trio Taylor Red who built a massive online following with her identical triplet sisters, died Sept. 28 after a battle with breast cancer. She was 35.
 Nika and Natalie Taylor announced her death in a video posted Nov. 2, saying they had hoped Nicole would recover and share her story herself.
 “This isn’t the video we thought we’d ever be making,” Natalie said. “We thought she would be here sharing her story of earthly healing, but instead we’re here sharing her story of heavenly healing.”
 Nicole, the pair said, was at peace and no longer suffering.
 In a memorial posted on Taylor Red’s website , they described Nicole, the eldest of the triplets by just minutes, as “our leader and our best friend.”
 “We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again,” they wrote. The family has held a private funeral service.
 Nicole was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer in 2022. The cancer was aggressive, and the news came as a shock to the family, her sisters said.
 In a 2023 interview with SurvivorNet , Nicole recalled finding a lump in her breast in February 2022 that felt like “a little AAA battery.”
 After a mammogram and exam, she was initially told to keep an eye on it and come back in six months. By the time she returned, she said, the lump had doubled or tripled in size. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis.
 Nicole, who said she had no family history of breast cancer, credited her faith and her medical team with helping her through it.
 Three days after she learned the news, family and friends began praying for her every day at 3:18 p.m., a nod to March 18, 1991, the triplets’ shared birthday.
 “I definitely believe God has worked miracles through this,” Nicole said in the 2023 interview, adding that she hoped to offer others “some hope and some positivity.”
 She was determined to live fully throughout her illness, even keeping up CrossFit during chemotherapy, Natalie said in the video.
 For a time, treatment appeared to be working. After Nicole finished chemo, she was told there was no evidence of disease. But the cancer later progressed to stage 4, according to the family.
 Through surgery and further treatment, she kept working, traveling and trying to enjoy life, and stayed hopeful even as her illness advanced.
 “She said, ‘We’re not going to live in dread during all of this,’” Natalie recalled.
 Growing up, the triplets played music together, learning guitar, banjo, fiddle and mandolin. They first performed as Red Roots before becoming Taylor Red.
 In an episode of the “ Hope Ignited ” podcast, the three discussed their music, their creative process and how Nicole’s diagnosis had strengthened their bond.
 But Nicole’s role in the trio extended far beyond music. As the oldest sister, she was often the one who took the lead, spoke up for her siblings and wasn’t afraid to stand her ground.
 “She was always the one who would speak on behalf of us,” Natalie recalled in the video announcing her death.
